label: prf:mass-coefficient-shadow-price
title: Proof of mass coefficient shadow price
html:
Proof. Proof of mass coefficient shadow price

Proof. The operator selection LP at Hecke level k selects the nuclear operator \Phi = \sum_i x_i b_i \in H_k(R, q) by:

  \min_x \; \sum_i t_i \, x_i
  \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
  \mathbf{1}^T x = n_{\mathrm{target}}, \;\;
  G x \geq 0

where t_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) and G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) is the Frobenius Gram matrix.

In the Wedderburn basis \{e^\lambda_{ij}\}, the Gram matrix block-diagonalises: G = \bigoplus_\lambda G_\lambda with G_\lambda = (w_\lambda / d_\lambda) \, I_{d_\lambda^2}, where w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2 / [k]_q! and d_\lambda = \dim(\lambda). The Frobenius constraint Gx \geq 0 separates into one constraint per partition \lambda:

  \langle \Phi, \pi_\lambda \rangle_F
  = \frac{w_\lambda}{d_\lambda} \, \mathrm{tr}(\Phi_\lambda)
  \geq 0

where \Phi_\lambda is the projection of \Phi onto the \lambda-block and \pi_\lambda is the central idempotent.

Dual program. The dual of the spectral LP is:

  \max_{u_0, \, u_\lambda \geq 0} \;\; n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0
  \text{s.t.} \quad
  u_0 + \frac{w_\lambda}{d_\lambda} \, u_\lambda
  \leq \frac{w_\lambda}{d_\lambda}
  \quad \forall \, \lambda \vdash k

By strong duality (the feasible set is non-empty and bounded), primal and dual optima coincide. The optimal dual variables u_\lambda^* satisfy complementary slackness:

  u_\lambda^* \cdot \langle \Phi^*, \pi_\lambda \rangle_F = 0

Factorisation. For the nuclear braid \Phi(Z,N), each dual variable factors as:

  u_\lambda^*(Z,N) = C_\lambda \cdot S_\lambda(Z,N,A)

where:

  1. C_\lambda is a q-integer product determined by the partition algebra (hooks, contents, Frobenius coordinates) — independent of any nuclear datum.

  2. S_\lambda(Z,N,A) is the scaling function determined by the content sum c(\lambda) = \sum_\square (j-i):

    • c(\lambda) > 0: volume-type (A-dependent)
    • c(\lambda) = 0: isospin-type (T(T+1)/A^p)
    • c(\lambda) < 0: charge-type (Z-dependent)

The factorisation is unique because the Wedderburn blocks are orthogonal under the Frobenius pairing: different partitions contribute to linearly independent scaling functions.

Mass-formula decomposition. The binding energy is:

  B(Z,N) = \sum_{\lambda} C_\lambda \cdot S_\lambda(Z,N,A)
           \cdot m_e

Each term of the QOU six-term mass formula is one shadow price u_\lambda^* (or the sum of a conjugate pair u_\lambda^* + u_{\lambda'}^* when \lambda' = \lambda^\vee). The coefficient C_\lambda \cdot m_e is the shadow price evaluated at the normalisation point where S_\lambda = 1.

Corollary (coefficient at each level). By the Markov-trace normalization \sum_\lambda d_\lambda\, y_\lambda(q) = 1, the per-level budget is set by the Hecke-level scale [k]_q! (the q-factorial at level k). This constrains the total shadow-price budget: the normalization is the dual feasibility constraint ensuring all u_\lambda^* are consistent. The budget at level k is [k]_q!; the marginal budget from advancing k \to k+1 is [k+1]_q! - [k]_q! = [k]_q! \cdot ([k+1]_q - 1).

Corollary (branching rule for coefficients). The branching \mathrm{Res}^{H_{k+1}}_{H_k} V_\mu = \bigoplus_{\lambda} V_\lambda induces a constraint on the level-(k{+}1) shadow prices via Frobenius reciprocity:

  C_\mu = \sum_{\lambda : \lambda \nearrow \mu}
    \frac{\dim_q(\mu)}
         {\sum_{\mu' : \lambda \nearrow \mu'} \dim_q(\mu')}
    \cdot C_\lambda

where \lambda \nearrow \mu denotes that \mu is obtained from \lambda by adding one cell. This propagates known coefficients from level k to level k{+}1 without fitting. \square
